restrictions: The two messages have 55 and 63 bytes: each is one chunk, one block, one root compression with flags 11, counter 0 and its true block length; the 63-byte message ends in eight zero bytes, so that in the zero-filled block of both messages the words 14 and 15 and the top byte of word 13 are zero.
Unkeyed BLAKE3-256 with 2 prefix rounds, standard IV, permutation and feed-forward, full 256-bit digest; an ordinary collision between two distinct complete messages.

Exact part: for every choice of eight 32-bit words the two digests agree on digest words 0, 2, 5 and 7, and one of the eight words is the round-1 state word Y4, which the search holds inside a class of 524,288 values. Heuristic part: a search over 2^102 such pairs, all with Y4 in the class, for one whose remaining 128 digest bits agree. The search works on batches of seven pairs and examines a batch further only if one of its pairs passes a filter on one internal word (rule A, five bit conditions); rule A is not implied by a collision, and a pair that fails it is examined further only if another pair of its batch passes, and is not counted in the success bound.

Classical 256-bit word RAM under collision-frontier-v5; seven trials per 256-bit word in 36-bit lanes on a 16-register load/store machine; a batch has two stages: every batch runs stage A, 55 operations (arithmetic, logical and shift operations, comparisons and branches) plus 32 loads, and only a batch in which a trial passes rule A runs stage 2, 115 operations plus 48 loads; with stage 2 counted for one quarter of the batches, and with the set-up per context and the last partial batch of every class loop, a trial is charged 19.1 operations; no sorting or lookup and no table that grows with the number of trials (one fixed list of 74,899 words holds the class members and is read in order); the algorithm halts with failure when 74,899 * 2^81 batches have run stage 2 (one quarter of the batches of a run) or when 2^86 trials that passed the second test have been processed.

Randomized by one fresh uniform 256-bit word. The success probability 0.39 holds only under heuristics H1, H2 and H3. The factor 2^25 = 33,554,432 in H1 is assumed and is not measured by the organizer-run experiments; with the uniform rate instead, the same search needs 2^127 trials and gives time_log2 122.6. No full 2-round collision is exhibited and none was computed.

Six 32-bit constants, the 32-bit word eta that defines the class and three 32-bit constants of rule A are stored in the program (40 bytes of advice); the six constants were found by a participant's solver search and chosen by a participant's count of the solutions of a seven-word system, and rule A was read off counts of the same kind; and recomputing the constants and selecting them, eta and rule A is bounded by 2^63 units and included in the time. memory_log2_bytes 35 covers the memory of that selection (below 2^34 bytes of main memory and below 10 GB of graphics-card memory, as observed by the participant); the search itself needs less than 2^22 bytes. No priority or novelty claim is made; the number of trials is 2^102 instead of 2^128 because a trial is assumed to succeed 33,554,432 times more often than a uniform 128-bit value would.

heuristics.statement: Over the algorithm's one random word, the 2^102 enumerated trials behave, with respect to the event that the 128-bit residual R is zero and the trial satisfies rule A, like independent events of probability at least 2^-103 each (2^25 = 33,554,432 times the rate of a uniform 128-bit value), to the extent that the probability that no trial has this event is at most exp(-1/2) + 0.002.
heuristics.scope: Exactly the trials of proof.md Section 6.4: lengths 55 and 63, the six constants of Section 3.2, the class of Y4 defined by eta = 830303cf (Lemma Q), contexts of seven words of which four come from the random word, two run over 2^51 pairs and one, X14, over all 2^32 values, and all 524,288 members of the class for every context. Rule A is the set of five bit conditions of Section 6.3 on the word h1 of a trial (Lemma A).
heuristics.extrapolation: From a participant count of the class rate under the seven-word model, that is of the number of solutions with Y4 in the class of the seven-word system that determines R. The count is an enumeration, without sampling except in seven small parts named below: for each value beta of an auxiliary difference of one of the two calls, every outcome of that call is enumerated, the other call is counted exactly for it, and the probability of the outcome is counted exactly. Over all 133,742 values of beta (4,550 enumerated in full by the calculator, the rest decided by a SAT solver on the whole system and counted where it found a solution), 60 have a nonzero part and the count is 162,266,764 times the uniform expectation; seven values of beta hold estimates, 0.28 together. Rule A is not implied by R = 0: three SAT solvers on two formulas found no solution violating it for 54 of the 453 outcomes of the count; the other 399 are left out in full, as are the seven values of beta that hold estimates, leaving 126,003,600. An exact count of the second call split by the rule, by a reviewing helper agent's program, finds no violating solution in the same 54 outcomes and gives 144,123,441 as the model's own value of the rate with rule A; the claim keeps the smaller figure. An independent recount by another AI model (GPT Sol 6.1) with a method and a program of its own, in integer arithmetic over every value of beta, gives 162,266,763.66 from the same 60 values; its program was run again here and its parts agree with the count for all 53 values counted in full. The other model had been told the participant's total, the four heaviest parts and the number of values with a part; the other 56 parts and the factors of the outcomes were not given to it. From checks of the counting program for these constants: both counts against the approximate model counter ApproxMC for the sixteen largest outcomes (largest difference 0.023 and 0.159 bits); both against brute force with 8-bit words (36,826 of 36,826 and 62,639 of 62,639 outcomes equal); and a sampler for the four heaviest values of beta (-0.05 standard errors for their sum). From a comparison of the seven-word model with real trials of the class search for these constants at 32 bits: 2^45 real trials against 2^44 draws from the model without a deviation beyond 2.55 standard deviations among 95 statistics; all real trials together (2^47.84) against exact expectations on four events of one call each, down to a probability of about 2^-40 (204 events against 206.0 expected); of the 51,093 listed partial events of the second call, 29,693 satisfy the first four conditions of rule A, where the model gives a share of 0.5809 (+0.10 standard deviations); and 24 runs with shared outer words. And from scaled-down end-to-end runs with 8-bit and 10-bit words, which exist only for the construction of the earlier submission c47c1a80 (lengths 60 and 62) and other constants (9,835 collisions against 9,837.9 predicted at 8 bits, 693 against 664.6 at 10 bits). All in proof.md Section 10. The extrapolation is from these to the rate of the event over 2^102 real trials.
heuristics.limitations: The factor 33,554,432 is assumed. It is set against a participant count of 126,003,600, 3.75 times larger, which the organizer-run experiments do not measure; the success bound needs a factor of at least 33,502,523. With factor 1 (the uniform rate) the claim would be 2^127 trials and time_log2 122.6. The count is exact only under the seven-word model, that six of the seven words behave like independent uniform words over the trials; that the trials of the algorithm meet the counted solutions at the model's rate is the assumption. The model does NOT hold inside one context for rule A: in a sample of 4,096 independent contexts the share of the trials of one context that satisfy its first four conditions lay between 0.66 and 1.38 times 2^-4 (other samples have values up to 1.46), with 138 times the variance of independent trials; only the average over contexts has the model's value, and whether the rate of trials that satisfy rule A and have R = 0 has the model's value on average was not measured and cannot be. The model is compared with real messages only for events of probability about 2^-40 and above; its use at the probability of a collision, about 2^-100.73, cannot be tested directly. No scaled-down end-to-end run exists for this length pair, for this construction of the trial or for a rule of this kind; the scaled-down runs quoted are for the earlier construction. Rule A is not implied by a collision; it gives up 22.35% of the count, and that it loses no more rests on solver answers and on an exact count of one call split by the rule, all made by the participant's helper agents; the solver answers have proofs that only a participant-side checker has accepted, no standard proof checker; rule A was chosen from counts of the same kind. No measurement tests rule A together with R = 0; the one that joins its first four conditions with a deep event of one call agrees with the model. The constants and the class were chosen to make the count large, by a solver search and by the count itself; the count is deterministic, so no sampling noise enters, but a choice that is best under the model says nothing about the model, and if the model overstates the rate for some constants such a search will tend to find them. The count rests on few paths: 44% of it comes from one value of beta and 77% from two. The counting program is not in the package; it and every check of it are the participant's; the independent recount is by another AI model, which had been told the total, and whose program was rerun and compared here but not reviewed line by line. All trials of a run share four seed words, the contexts of one pair share most of their words, the 2^19 pairs with the same difference of the two enumerated words give, for each value of the third, messages that differ in four words only, and the 524,288 trials of one context differ only in Y4 and what follows from it; their independence is assumed, and no measurement has the structure of these groups of pairs. Real trials in a layout with shared outer words exist on the graphics card only as 24 runs of 2^40 trials, each a share 2^-11 of the work for one pair of enumerated words, and eight more with the third enumerated word spread out; the ratio of variance to mean of the early-test passes of the 24 is 1.28 (first eight alone 2.23). The proofs of the new construction lemmas (S, F, Y) and this whole text were written by helper agents of the participant and were reviewed once, by three further helper agents of the same AI model and by no person. Nothing here is organizer-verified except the two declared experiments, which do not measure the 128-bit rate and are not a test of H1.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than 2^86 of the 2^102 trials pass the 32-bit E1 test of proof.md Lemma N without having R = 0.
heuristics.scope: The E1 test of Section 6.3 on all trials of Section 6.4, whether or not their batch runs stage 2; the algorithm processes only the passes in batches that run stage 2, which are fewer. The measured pass rate 2^-31.39 would give 2^70.6 passes; the budget of 2^86 corresponds to a pass rate of 2^-16 and is larger by a factor of about 2^15.3, and processing 2^86 passes is charged in the time bound (2^96 operations).
heuristics.extrapolation: From participant measurements of the pass rate on real trials with these constants at 32 bits (77,238 passes in 2^47.62 trials with independent random contexts, against 8,242 in 2^44.39 draws from the model; 9,520 passes in 24 runs of 2^40 trials laid out with shared outer words; all in proof.md Section 10, where a pass of the E1 test is called a trial in which E1 requires the class) to the 2^102 trials of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The measured rate is a mean; that the pass count of a full run of 2^102 trials, whose contexts share four seed words, stays near that mean is assumed. The layout runs cover 2^21 of the 2^32 values of X14 of one pair each and do not share seed words with each other. The budget exceeds the passes expected at the measured rate by a factor of about 2^15.3. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H2 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005.

heuristics.statement: With probability at least 0.9995 over the random word, fewer than 74,899 * 2^81 of the 2^102 trials satisfy rule A of proof.md Section 6.3, so that fewer than that many batches run stage 2.
heuristics.scope: Rule A (Lemma A) on the trials of Section 6.4, in the seven-lane batches of Section 6.5. A batch runs stage 2 only if one of its seven trials satisfies rule A, and every trial lies in one batch, so the number of batches that run stage 2 is at most the number of trials that satisfy rule A. The budget is one quarter of the 74,899 * 2^83 batches of a run, a share 2^-4.81 of the trials, 1.142 times 2^-5; the time bound charges stage 2 for that many batches, and the algorithm halts with failure when the budget is reached. The statement is about the total over the 2^83 contexts of a run, that is about the average share over contexts; it is not claimed context by context. What the algorithm budgets is batches, and the statement on trials is a sufficient condition for it; the measured share of the batches that hold a trial satisfying rule A is 0.1216 for random contexts and 0.1133 in the ranges of the algorithm, less than half the budget.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the fact that a uniform 32-bit word satisfies the five conditions of rule A with probability 2^-5, and from participant measurements on real trials at 32 bits: in 2,048 random contexts with all members (1,073,741,824 trials, on the processor) 33,485,196 trials satisfy rule A, a share of 2^-5.0030, and a share of 0.1216 of the batches hold such a trial; in 2,048 contexts laid out in the ranges of the algorithm (eight sets of seed words, the second enumerated word below 2^19, consecutive values of the third) the two shares are 2^-5.0008 and 0.1133; the largest share of the batches of one context in all samples is 0.1684, against the budget of 0.25; two programs that reviewing helper agents wrote from the proof text give 0.9988 and 0.9977 times 2^-5 for independent contexts and means from 0.9926 to 1.0065 for 12 sets of shared seed words; on the graphics card, where only the first four conditions are recorded, 2^47.62 trials with independent contexts give 13,537,739,903,614 against 13,537,736,916,992 expected at 2^-4, and each of 32 runs of 2^40 trials with shared outer words is within 6 parts in 100,000 of 2^-4. The self-test of the submitted program finds a share of that size among the lanes of its own inputs (456 of 14,000 lanes, and 218,402 of 7,000,000 in a longer run). All in proof.md Sections 6.5 and 10. The extrapolation is from these averages over sampled contexts to the average over the contexts of one run.
heuristics.limitations: Not organizer-verified. The share of the trials of ONE context that satisfy rule A is not 2^-5: in a sample of 4,096 independent contexts the share of the trials of one context that satisfy its first four conditions lay between 0.66 and 1.38 times 2^-4 (other samples have values up to 1.46), with 138 times the variance of independent trials. Only the average over contexts is, and a context at the upper end exceeds the budget on its own trials (in no sample on its own batches). That the average over the contexts of one run, which share four seed words and, in groups of 2^32, two more words, is not 1.142 times the mean is assumed. The fifth condition of rule A was measured only on the processor, in runs of 2^29 to 2^32 trials; no run on the graphics card records it. If the budget were exceeded the algorithm halts with failure, which lowers the success probability but does not raise the time bound; H3 enters the success bound only through its own failure probability of 0.0005. The operation counts of the two stages are the submitted program's own.
